items_missed: No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — not once, on a call where the customer twice named an antique piece as her single concern and said 'the only item that we normally worry about is that one antique piece.' The $2,000 coverage was the answer to the exact worry she handed over.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — she gave an 8:30-9:00 ETA and stopped there, with no 'if we miss that window we start discounting immediately.'
No insurance explanation of any kind — no No Worries, no 60c/lb baseline. Third-time customer moving an antique and it never came up.

Washer/dryer disconnect and reconnect quoted as 'additional fees' with no dollar amount. That is an unpriced line item sitting inside a quote she otherwise built carefully, and it will show up on the invoice as a surprise.
No agenda statement. 'Do you mind if we talk about it a little bit more?' is a permission ask, not a roadmap — no gather-details-then-pricing structure, no 10-15 minute timeframe, no 'sound good?'
Customer asked 'How are you?' and Amy never answered or reciprocated — went straight into the audio troubleshooting.

Pricing recited badly. '$206 92 $192 mm-hmm mm-hmm we get the same $14' and 'Oh, sorry $920,206 is the hours for two for a Saturday' forced the customer to stop and ask 'The 292 you said was for...?' The most important numbers in the call were the least clear.
'Pricing is super simple' opener not used — she went with 'Let's start with the basic pricing.'
What's-included list incomplete: named the 26-foot truck, pads, dolly and tools, but not gas, taxes or insurance.
No-hidden-fees pitch attempted but truncated and garbled — 'no credit card fees, no stair. Well no we already assembly fees' — no transportation fee, no fuel surcharge.
No clock-start explanation ('clock starts on site when the contract opens') and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the pricing or the estimate.

Save Your Ass delivered as a fragment. She landed the time-equals-money point but supplied no consolidation examples of her own (kids' toys, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), never pitched 'take a carload,' and never closed with 'does that make sense?' The customer generated the Saturday-self-move idea and the garden-furniture example herself.
Never asked about access at either end — parking, driveway, truck placement, HOA. She is moving into a house the customer just closed on and has never seen.
Destination address and zip never captured or confirmed on the call; origin referenced only loosely as 'June Barry' / 'June Berry.' No storage stops or additional stops question.
No walk distance at either home — a variable that helped drive last year's 11.5-hour actual.
Divorce disclosure got a rushed 'Okay, is this sorry to hear about that' and an immediate pivot to the Sunday rate.
Email handoff mentioned but not explained — no bolded detail list at the top, no 'reply with any corrections.' Redirected to a phone call instead. No business hours given.
top_strength: Amy did the thing almost nobody does: she built the estimate from real history instead of a guess. She pulled the prior contract and put the number on the table — 'I checked your contract from last year and says here we sent you two movers one truck and it took them eleven and a half hours' — then asked the customer to help explain it, then reasoned forward out loud, subtracting the 22 bins and 10 boxes the customer was self-handling and weighing the two-story-to-two-story stairs, to land on 'we can do this still with two movers but I would suggest budgeting maybe around six to eight hours, just to be a bit conservative.' She then dollarized both ends of the range with the travel fee baked in ($1,222 at six hours, $1,606 at eight), so the customer knew her real exposure, not just a rate. On top of that she proactively steered the customer to Sunday to save $14/hour when she didn't have to, and she closed with a deliberate, well-framed stressor question: 'a very important question for me. What are you most concerned about for this move... I wanna make sure we address everything.' The call ended booked, with no deposit, and the customer thanking her by name.
coaching_note: Amy, this is a strong call with one expensive hole in the middle of it: you never said the words 'No Worries Damage Coverage.' The customer told you twice that the antique piece is the one thing she worries about — that is the single best opening for our coverage pitch you will get all month, and it went by. Next time, the moment a customer names a worry item, go straight there: 'That's exactly what our No Worries Damage Coverage is for — every move includes up to $2,000 to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage, so that antique is protected, and on top of that we go heavy on the wrap.' You already said the wrap half; the coverage half is what turns a worry into a reason to book with us. Second priority is the other two differentiators, which are pure freebies on this call — you gave her an 8:30-9:00 ETA, so add 'and that's backed by our On-Time Guarantee: if we miss that window we start discounting immediately,' and since she's a third-time customer who praised the crews, Meet Your Mover practically sells itself: 'a few days out you'll get an email with your mover's photo and info, so you know who's coming.' Third, slow down on the numbers. The Saturday-versus-Sunday comparison came out as a jumble and she had to ask you to repeat it. Say one rate, stop, confirm, then the other: 'Saturday is $206 an hour for two movers. Sunday is $192 — that's $14 an hour cheaper. Does Sunday work?' Last thing, and it's small: your Save Your Ass instinct was right but you left it half-built. She got to the take-a-carload idea on her own — own that pitch instead, with the specifics (loose items in drawers, toys, photos off the walls, anything that fits in the car), and close it with 'does that make sense?' Get those in and this call is a 65-plus.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and specific — used the customer's name three times at deliberate moments, thanked her for being thorough, volunteered the cheaper day 'to our clients to save a little,' and drew real reciprocity, with the customer disclosing personal news, praising past crews unprompted, and signing off 'Thank you so much Amy'; held back from a 5 by never answering the customer's 'how are you?' and by brushing past the divorce disclosure to get to price.
audio_review_reason: Documented line-quality failure plus a garbled delivery of the key numbers. The customer said 'It's a little worse actually' after Amy's fix attempt, and the Saturday/Sunday rate recitation came through as '$206 92 $192' and '$920,206' with the customer asking for a repeat — pull the audio to confirm she actually heard $206 / $192 / $70 travel fee / $1,222-$1,606 correctly before the confirmation email locks those numbers in, and to check whether the connection degraded further after the transcript's last flag.
